body:
N-26 SLICE 1 IS BUILT, NOT WALKED, NOT MARKED (helper-n26, 14 Nov 2026). The item is NOT complete: RELEASE-CANDIDATE.md 4b needs slices 1 AND 2 in the first public image, so I did not run `roadmap.py mark`. Slice 2 is not opened.

WHAT SLICE 1 DOES: imports/uploads.py is the one door (read_declared / read_official_video / read_upload); readers._read_entry gates on videoType (ATV, OFFICIAL_SOURCE_MUSIC and removed entries declared; OMV read_official_video; UGC, anything unknown, an available entry with no videoType and no album = an upload); the yt-dlp reader calls read_upload. Whole-name Unicode channel test (never a substring), every dash + middle dot + bullet, brackets never decide. Track carries artist_basis and uploader IN MEMORY ONLY. Proof: tests/test_import_upload_reading.py on 9 recorded YouTube Music search answers (tests/fixtures/ytm/n26; the playlist shape around them is constructed from playlist_album.json: no get_playlist of an upload was recorded), the invariance test over every recorded playlist (146 ATV + 1 OMV + 2 removed + 10 album: all unchanged, all declared), and mutation checks (12 guards, each one fails named tests).

FOR SLICE 2 (what it must do beyond the design):
1. THE FOURTH BASIS `unknown`: a song nobody names (the recorded OMV `Akudama` has EMPTY artists; a Spotify track may too) has artist "" and basis `unknown` in the reader; ImportService._song_of files it under the placeholder "Unknown Artist" (the keeper's folder name) so that one song no longer refuses a whole import (it did: "A song needs a title and an artist."). artist_finder's skip must treat `unknown` EXACTLY like `channel`: otherwise "Unknown Artist" gets catalogue picture look-ups from the Host's address. Persist artist_basis `unknown` on the ref too.
2. refs.find: two different videos with the placeholder artist, the same title and a compatible length share a norm_key and resolve to ONE ref (the first one's video). Rare, and the same hazard as any two same-named songs; slice 2 may want the video id to win over the name when both refs hold different video ids.
3. The OMV rule keeps the artist's name in the song title as today ("Metallica - One (Live) [...]" stays the title); a later cleanup may strip it.

KNOWN LEFTOVERS (all pinned by named tests, all under N-28): an OMV credited to a LABEL with no separator in its title (Pure Noise Records / Vomit Forth) keeps the label; an upload whose title names nobody keeps its uploader flagged `channel` (David C / Metallica One Music Video with Lyrics HQ); `Lionel Messi * Monaco - Bad Bunny` is read artist-first (U2); ARTE Concert and Crunchyroll stay under their channels until slice 4 (flagged `channel`). The OMV rule can misread `Song - Subtitle` under a band's credit (neither side is the credit, no version word).

DECISION I TOOK (yours to overrule): an OMV whose title says the credited name ANYWHERE keeps the credit even when neither side of the separator is that name. Real case recorded: `DANDADAN Opening in ITALIANO - EXTENDED "Otonoke" Creepy Nuts | ItsKlyo` is typed OMV and credited to ItsKlyo; the rule as first worded (neither side names the credit => read the title) made "DANDADAN Opening in ITALIANO" an artist with basis `title`. Cost: a label credit repeated in the title also stays (the same unknowable case as above).

HOUSEKEEPING: AUDIT-BUILT-2026-11-05.md had TWO B-125 rows and TWO B-126 rows on main (a merge residue of #72/#74). In this PR the register keeps ONE B-125 row (updated: slice 1 built, row stays open) and ONE B-126 row (the newest text, with N-27 slice 2a from #77); both stale duplicates are deleted (resolving a merge conflict with #77, the stale B-126 one was dropped for the same reason).

WHERE THIS NOTE LIVES: it is committed in the N-26 slice 1 PR (docs/roadmap/notes/N-26/), not written into encore-live, so it appears on the board when that PR is merged.
